The prayer is “O God, who [came] to souls.” The reading is “Hear, O Israel.” The responsory is “Turn back, O Lord.” The prayer is “Grant, we ask, almighty God.”

The reading is “The Lord said to Moses.” The responsory is “Let my prayer be directed.” The prayer is “Grant, we ask, almighty…”

The reading is “The angel of the Lord descended.” Two brothers in white are to say the shorter blessing: “Blessed are you, O Lord,” continuing until “Let heaven, earth, sea, and all that is in them bless you.”

Then let them repeat it, followed by “And worthy of praise.” “Glory to the Father” [Col. 1217C] is to be said with the repetition “And worthy of praise,” and then they are to continue: “As it was.” “And worthy of praise,” with those mentioned above responding “Blessed are you.”

As soon as this has been said, let the priest come to the altar and say “The Lord be with you.” The collect is “O God, who [did this] three times.” The epistle is “Therefore, having been justified.” The tract is “Praise,” likewise sung by two men in white.

The Gospel is “As Jesus went out.” The offertory is “O God, God of my salvation.” The communion is “I will not leave you orphans.”

## CHAPTER XIII. The Octave of Pentecost

The invitatory is “Alleluia, the Spirit of the Lord,” sung by two men in cappas. Three candlesticks are to be placed before the altar and one behind it.

At the Nocturns, single antiphons [Col. 1217D] are to be said with “Alleluia,” from the feast itself. The eight readings are from a sermon of Saint Leo, pope. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth responsories are to be sung by two men.

The homily is from the Gospel “There was a man of the Pharisees,” with the exposition of Gregory Nazianzen. At Lauds the antiphon is “Alleluia, when they were being completed.” At the Gospel the antiphon is “A man came to Jesus by name.”

If any feast occurs on this day, they are to repeat the antiphon and celebrate the morning Mass, adding the collect “O God, who on this day…” If the Holy Spirit has not yet arrived, they are to perform one collect at the sacred service, with the preface of Easter Day.

The procession is to be made as on the preceding Sundays. However, when they return to the atrium before the church doors, let them begin the antiphon “Crucified [Col. 1218A] in the flesh,” with the repetitions “Do not…” As they enter, let them sing the antiphon “Today they were completed.”

At Mass everyone is to be clad in cappas. Seven candlesticks are to be placed before the altar and three behind it. The office is “The Spirit of the Lord.” The prayer is “O God, who on this day…” The epistle is “I saw an open door.” The first Alleluia is “I will not leave you”; the second Alleluia is “Come, Holy Spirit.” The Gospel is “There was a man of the Pharisees.” The offertory is “Confirm this, O God.” The communion is “It was made.”

At the conclusion of the sacred service, all the bells are to be rung.

At vespers the antiphon is “Alleluia, they were filled.” The antiphon at the Gospel is “Today they were completed, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Today all the apostles…”

## CHAPTER XIV. The Second Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 1218B]

During the weekdays of that week, let them sing the office “Lord, in your mercy.” The prayer is “O God of those who hope in you.” The Gospel is “There was a certain rich man.”

From this point until the Ides of September they are to fast on Wednesday and Friday, as our Father Benedict instituted in chapter 47 of his Rule. The abbot is to exercise the discretion that the most blessed teacher himself commanded, on account of the fainthearted, inclement weather, or if the labor of that place should have become too great.

If the abbot or prior decides that they are to eat, let them proceed as follows. As soon as they have risen from Chapter and come into the cloister, at the abbot’s command let the lesser bell be sounded, so that the kitchen servers and the other brothers may prepare everything that must be prepared [Col. 1218C]. Let them celebrate Mass at Terce and eat at Sext.

If they fast, then immediately after Sext, as soon as the midday sleepers have risen [perhaps from *meridiana*, that is, from the sleep after midday], let the boys come before the altar to pray. When this has been done, let them begin the antiphon “Arise, O Lord.” Then let them make the procession in order, as we have frequently prescribed.

Let the Gospels be read on weekdays as they are found written in the sacramentary. On Friday they must sing a Mass in honor of the holy Cross; and if a saint’s feast occurs, so that three readings are made, let them sing the Mass of that saint.

When no saint’s feast occurs, let the Gospel of that day, “There was a certain rich man,” be read on Thursday. Throughout that week they are to sing at the Magnificat antiphons from the Gospel “There was a certain rich man.”

On Saturday at vespers the responsory is “Prepare your hearts.” At the Magnificat the antiphon is “Mountains of Gilboa.”

## CHAPTER XV. The Third Sunday after Pentecost

Let them say the invitatory “Let us go before.” The hymn is “Rising at night.” Let them read eight lessons from the Books of Kings. The responsory is “God of all.”

In the third [supplement: Nocturn], the homily is from the Gospel “There was a certain rich man.” Let them sing the responsories from that same story until the Kalends of August.

At the morning Hour the hymn is “Behold, now the night.” Until the Kalends of October [Col. 1219A], let them read *Malachim* and *Verba dierum* in the refectory [Note: [Col. 1219D] *Malachim*, plural of the Hebrew *Melech*, means the Book of Kings. *Verba dierum* is a subdivision of the Books of Kings].

On weekdays, therefore, at the Gospel canticle of the Magnificat, we sing by turns each day both the historical and Gospel antiphons that follow. On the other Sundays that follow, likewise let eight readings be read at the nocturnal services from the Books of Kings, until the Kalends of August.

## CHAPTER XVI. Here Begins a Rhythm Adorned with Sacred Doctrine

When the fast of the four seasons occurs after the octave of Pentecost, let Wednesday and Friday be celebrated as regular fast days. They may speak in the cloister after Chapter until Terce.

After Sext, when they hear the signal, let them rise from their beds and, barefoot [Col. 1219B], proceed to wash their hands and faces. Let both they and the boys go into the church without any sound. After they have prayed, let the boys begin the antiphon “Arise, O Lord,” and let them do the rest that is required there; let them sing the litany.

On Saturday, however, they are not to perform the litany before the principal Mass. At the sacred service, let the offertory, prayers, and everything else be done as prescribed below in this book for the week of Pentecost, and as we have found them written in the sacramentary and in authoritative copies, so that they are to be performed.

At the meal the almoner is to receive whatever remains for the brothers. They are not to eat fat. As they leave, each person is to read in silence.

On these two days, after vespers has been sung, immediately after they have left the dormitory, let the church keeper sound the bell until the boys assemble and perform the Office of the Dead. On the other days, when they have eaten twice, let them do this immediately after the refectory servers have left the refectory.

## CHAPTER XVII. Saint John the Baptist Requires These Practices

On the Vigil of the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist, immediately after the signal has sounded following Sext, let them rise from their beds, attend to their personal needs, wash their hands and faces, and go to the oratory without the sound of metal. Let them pray, and let the boy immediately begin the litany.

Let them celebrate Mass as it is contained in the sacramentary. At its completion let the signal be sounded, while they pray. The servers are to go and receive the mixed drink; afterward the signal is to be sounded again, and they are to complete the Hour.

Whatever remains in the refectory on that day is to be received by the almoner. They are not to eat fat on this day. While they are sitting at table, the church keeper is to adorn the church, presbytery, and choir, and the altars with silk cloths [*gliphaticis*] [Note: [Col. 1220D] *Gliphaticus*, *glisaticus*, *glizaticus*: from *glizum*, *glisdum*, linen or a more valuable kind of cloth. See Du Cange, *Glossarium Latinitatis*].

Twelve candles are to be placed before the altar and eight behind it.

At vespers, one bell is to be sounded first. The chapter reading is “Before I formed you.” The responsory is “The Lord’s forerunner.” The hymn is “So that they may sing.” The versicle is “For he will be great before the Lord.”

Two priests are to put on cappas. Let them surround the altars with incense [Col. 1220A]. The antiphon “When Zacharias entered” is to be repeated twice. The prayer is “Grant, we ask, almighty God,” as above.

At the station the responsory is “Among those born.” The prayer is “Of him.”

For the invitatory, four men are to put on cappas. The hymn is “So that they may sing.” The eight readings are from a sermon of Saint Augustine: “The solemnity of this day requires a solemn…” In the third watch the Gospel is “Elizabeth was fulfilled.” The homily is by Saint Ambrose, bishop.

The brothers are to pronounce the responsories two by two together; the twelfth is to be repeated from the beginning after the “Glory.”

At the canticle: “Blessed is the man who is in wisdom.” At Lauds the short responsory is “Behold, I have given my words.” The hymn is “The others only…”

At the morning Mass, “The righteous will flourish like the palm” is used, and only this prayer is to be said: “Grant, we ask, almighty God.”

The reading from Isaiah is “To Zion: Behold, I am here.” The responsory is “The righteous will flourish like the palm.” The Alleluia is “You, child.” The Gospel is “Zacharias said to the angels,” continuing to “To remove my reproach.” The offertory is “Glory and honor.” The communion is “You are great.”

At the principal Mass, everyone is to be dressed in cappas, including the unlearned (*idiotae*: the uneducated, who have not learned letters); all the children (*pueri toti*, that is, all of them, from Italian *tutti*) are to have tunics on.

Let nine men perform the office, one the Gradual, and six the Alleluia. At the sequence let two large bells be rung together. At the abbot’s command, two persons are to perform the offering.

In the refectory let the general meal and the *pitantia* be given. Let the drink be served once.

At vespers let them use the antiphons that they sang above at the Nocturns, and take the psalms from the office of one martyr. The responsory is “Kings will see,” or “Elizabeth of Zacharias” [Col. 1220C]. The hymn is “O life-giving prophet.”

### Within the Octave

They are not to bend their knees within the octave. The invitatory is “The King of the Forerunner.” Let them appoint antiphons in the first and second Nocturns. Let them read lessons from sermons of the Fathers. Let the responsories be from that same blessed [supplement: feast of John the Baptist].

The familiar psalms are not to be sung in this service, nor any other psalm for the dead. Instead, let the signal be sounded immediately and let them perform morning Lauds under one antiphon. Afterward let them come into another choir and sing the matins of All Saints and of the dead.

At Prime the psalm is “Have mercy on me, O God.” Then let them celebrate the Mass for the dead. In the cloister they may speak both before Terce and after None. At the Hours they are to omit the familiar psalms.

At Terce let the signal be sounded; let them pray together, and afterward let those who are to celebrate Mass put on white. When the signal has been sounded again, let them celebrate Terce. From this point let there be the litany.

At Mass the collect is “Grant, we ask,” together with the customary collects. The epistle is “Listen, islands.” The Gospel is “Elizabeth was fulfilled,” and the other elements are as they are contained in the sacramentary.

At the Hours let them appoint the antiphons that were used at Lauds. At vespers let them use those that were said at the Nocturn, and the weekday psalms as they occur day by day. If a saint’s feast occurs during this celebration, let them perform the office from that saint.

At the readings let them sing the invitatory. The hymn is “So that they may sing” [Col. 1221A]. After each Nocturn let them appoint one antiphon from blessed John and read the lessons from him. Let them sing the responsories from the saint, likewise at Lauds.

Let there be five antiphons at Lauds, and afterward let them repeat the antiphon of Saint John. At Prime let them say the Mass for the dead. At Terce let them celebrate the Mass of the saints, adding the collect from the Baptist and the other collects. After the completion of Mass, let them perform everything from the glorious John.

### The Octave of the Same Glorious John

Let them dress in white. For the invitatory, two brothers are to sing “The King himself, the Forerunner.” The hymn is “So that they may sing.”

Let the antiphons and responsories be performed by everyone as they were celebrated at his Nativity, except for the shortened responsories: at the “Glory to the Father,” the boys are to sing.

First: “Behold, I have given my words.” [Col. 1221B] Second: “Kings will see.” Third: “Elizabeth of Zacharias.”

The eight readings are “And it happened on the eighth day.” In the third, the homily is from the Gospel “Elizabeth was fulfilled.”

After the Gospel reading let them say this prayer: “Grant, we ask, almighty God.” At Lauds let them appoint five antiphons. Then let them repeat the antiphon with the “Glory” from the apostles.

Let them celebrate the morning Mass of the holy apostles. At the principal office, “From my mother’s womb,” as it was at his feast. The collect is “Grant, we ask, almighty God,” and let them sing the sequence.

At vespers the antiphons are those they sang earlier in the first Nocturn. The psalm is from the feast of one martyr. The responsory is “Elizabeth.” The hymn is “O life-giving prophet.” The antiphon is “The light that you see with the mind.” The prayer is from him [Col. 1221C], and afterward let them repeat the antiphon of the apostles.

## CHAPTER XVIII. The Vigil of Saint Paul

Thus the observance honors the apostolic feast.

Before Prime let them adorn the entire church in order, as it was on the day of the Nativity of the Lord. Let them celebrate the morning Mass of Saint Leo, pope.

The office is “He established him.” The prayer is from Saint Leo, together with the collect of blessed John and the other customary collects for the living, adding “of your saints” at the end.

The epistle is “Behold, a great priest.” The Gospel is “Watch, be vigilant, and pray.” Let everyone make the offering.

After Sext, as soon as they hear the signal, let them rise from their beds, wash their hands and faces, and let the boys go into the church without the sound of any bell. Let them pray.

The priest is to put on the chasuble, the deacon the dalmatic, and the subdeacon the tunic. The singers are to be in the choir with a cappa. Three conversi are to be in white; two of them are to carry candles and the censer. All the children are to be in white. Two brothers in cappas are to perform the responsory, and then all the bells are to be rung.

Office: “The Lord said to Peter” (*Dixit Dominus Petro*). Prayer: “Grant, we beseech you, almighty God” (*Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus*). Responsory: “Into all the earth” (*In omnem terram*). Offertory: “But to me exceedingly” (*Mihi autem nimis*). They shall carry the Gospel book to everyone; all shall approach for the kiss of peace. In the refectory the tables shall be covered; everyone shall have the general portion, as well as the *pitantia*, whatever kind of day it may have turned out to be. No suet shall be eaten on that day. Charity shall be poured out for everyone, and whatever remains of the bread and wine shall be received by the almoner. At Vespers two bells shall be rung together. Twelve candles shall be placed before the altar. The antiphon at Vespers: “You shall be blessed” (*Beati eritis*); the psalms shall be those for the day itself. Reading: “Peter indeed” (*Petrus quidem*). Responsory: “If you love me” (*Si diligis me*). Three or four brothers shall sing the hymn before the altar, “Felix through all things” (*Felix per omnes*), and it shall be sung only at this synaxis. Two priests shall put on copes to carry incense. Antiphon: “You are Peter” (*Tu es Petrus*), and afterward this shall be explained triumphally. “Let us pray: O God who [founded] your church” (*Deus qui ecclesiam tuam*), and they shall repeat the antiphon concerning Saint John. At Compline they shall begin this verse: “You just judges of the world” (*Vos saeculi justi judices*); let it be said at all the Hours up to the octave.

Before the nocturnal office, the whole church shall be illuminated. All the bells shall be rung together [Col. 1222B] until the boys arrive. Four in copes shall say the invitatory, “Let us adore Christ, King of kings” (*Christum Regem regum adoremus*), or “You are the shepherd of the sheep” (*Tu es pastor ovium*). Hymn: “Let heaven rejoice” (*Exsultet coelum*). Eight readings from a sermon of Saint Leo, pope, “The solemnity of all the saints” (*Omnium quidem sanctorum solemnitatem*). At the third vigil, a homily of Saint Jerome: “This Philip is the brother of Herod” (*Philippus iste est frater Herodis*). Three readings. After the twelfth has been read, [readings] of Saint Hilary, bishop, “In the progress of the discourse” (*In processu sermonis*). For the third reading, a priest shall be in a cope to incense only the great altar and the choir. The two responsories shall be sung by two and two together; at “Glory to the Father,” more singers shall be added, and after the Gloria they shall begin again from the beginning.

After the readings have been completed, the Gospel: “Jesus came” (*Venit Jesus*). Collect for the morning praises. Responsory: “Whatever” (*Quodcunque*). Hymn: “With golden light” (*Aurea luce*). Antiphon: “Whatever” (*Quodcunque*) [Col. 1222C]. “Let us pray,” and the antiphon concerning the Forerunner.

No other morning Mass shall be celebrated except that which the priests sing for the people at the altars. But as soon as they have left the chapter meeting, the church custodian shall sound the small bell. The boys shall go out, wash their hands, and proceed to the church. Then the sacristan shall sound the bell again until they come to pray. When this has been done, everyone, both young and old, shall put on white garments. Then the bell shall be sounded and they shall celebrate Terce. At that point they shall take the processional ornaments, as on the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ. The armarius shall impose the antiphon “When Peter was being led away” (*Dum duceretur Petrus*), and thus the procession shall begin; they shall leave in orderly fashion through the cloisters as they came. When they have reached the atrium, they shall prepare themselves [Col. 1222D] in the choir, as is customary. The cantor shall begin this antiphon: “Peter was led away” (*Ducti sunt Petrus*). From there they shall begin the responsory “You are the shepherd of the sheep” (*Tu es pastor ovium*) and enter the basilica. Then, while all the bells are ringing, the sacristan shall give copes to all the brothers and tunics to the boys. The office shall be assigned to twelve. Four responsories and six alleluias shall be performed at the ambo.

Two shall perform the office. At the beginning of the sacred office, twelve candles shall be lit before the altar. At the explanation of the Mass, all the bells shall be rung.

In the refectory everything shall be prepared as at Easter, and the same distribution of drink shall be made. At Vespers the antiphon shall be “The Lord has sworn” (*Juravit Dominus*), and the others as is customary on the Nativity of the apostles [Col. 1223A]. Responsory: “The apostle Peter and Paul” (*Petrus apostolus et Paulus*). Hymn: “Felix through all things” (*Felix per omnes*). “Let us pray: O God, who bestowed [gifts] upon your apostle Peter” (*Deus qui apostolo tuo Petro collatis*). Then they shall repeat [the office] concerning Saint Paul. Antiphon with Gloria. His prayer; and afterward [the office] concerning Saint John. If this feast falls on a Sunday, they shall make a procession as they did at the Resurrection.

## CHAPTER XIX. On the feast of Saint Paul

On the feast of Saint Paul, two shall be in copes for the invitatory. Hymn: “Let heaven rejoice” (*Exsultet coelum*). In the first and second nocturns, readings from the holy Fathers: “My little children, hear us and deliver yourselves” (*Filioli mei, audite nos, et liberate vos*). Responsory: “He who worked through Peter” (*Qui operatus est Petro*). The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be begun again from the beginning after the Gloria.

At the Lauds, hymn: “Outstanding teacher” (*Doctor egregie*) [Col. 1223B]. His antiphon and prayer; and afterward [the office] concerning Saint Peter, with Gloria. Then [the office] concerning John the Baptist.

For the morning Mass, [the Mass] of Saint Peter: “Now I truly know” (*Nunc scio vere*). Collect: “Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that by no [evils]” (*Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus, ut nullis*), and [the collect] of John the Baptist, together with the others. At the main office everyone shall be surrounded by copes, and the boys by tunics. Six shall hold the office. Epistle: “I make known to you my Gospel” (*Notum facio vobis Evangelium meum*). Four shall sing the Gradual. Six shall sing the Alleluia. At the end of Mass all the bells shall be sounded.

At the Hours, the antiphons that are from Lauds shall be brought forth without the succeeding verses. At Vespers, the antiphons from the nocturn shall be said without the verses. First: “He who worked through Peter” (*Qui operatus est Petro*), and the others. Responsory: “You are a chosen vessel” (*Tu es vas electionis*). Hymn: “Outstanding teacher” (*Doctor egregie*). Afterward they shall repeat the antiphon concerning Saint John [Col. 1223C], then that concerning the apostle Peter. On the following day they shall celebrate the octave of Saint John, as we have inserted above.

On the day before the Mass [perhaps: of the month] of July, a full office shall be performed for seven days for all our household members, as is customary for our brothers in November [supplement: “in the month”].

During the octave of these apostles they shall act as follows. They shall not kneel. Invitatory: “King of the apostles” (*Regem apostolorum*). Hymn: “Let heaven rejoice” (*Exsultet coelum*). From the psalms they shall take those concerning the apostles that are suitable, or from the history of the Prince of the Apostles, choosing those that agree with one another. Readings shall be from sermons of the holy Fathers. The first responsory shall be of the chief apostle, the second of Saint Paul, and the third of blessed Peter.

They shall take no psalm after the nocturns, but shall immediately sound the bell and celebrate Lauds from dawn, imposing this antiphon: “This is my commandment” (*Hoc est praeceptum meum*). Hymn: “With golden light” (*Aurea luce*). Then, in the other choir, they shall sing the Lauds of All Saints and of the dead: “O God, our ears have heard” (*Deus auribus nostris*), with five psalms for the anniversaries of the brothers.

At Prime, a Mass for the dead. In the cloister they shall speak as on other days; at the Hours, however, the antiphon of the many apostles. When fewer [apostles’ days] occur, they shall bring forth [antiphons] from the proper offices; likewise the chapters and prayers. The psalms for household members shall not be imposed.

After Terce they shall celebrate Mass. Office: “But to me” (*Mihi autem*). “Let us pray: O God, whose right hand” (*Deus cujus dextera*). Epistle: “You are no longer strangers” (*Jam non estis hospites*). Responsory: “Exceedingly honored” (*Nimis honorati*). Alleluia: “I have chosen you” (*Ego vos elegi*) [Col. 1224A]. Gospel: “This is my commandment” (*Hoc est praeceptum meum*). Office: “Into all the earth” (*In omnem terram*). Communion: “You who followed me” (*Vos, qui secuti estis me*).

At Vespers, the antiphon that is above the Gospel and is common to both, with the ferial psalms. After Terce they shall celebrate the Office of the Dead as usual. If a saint’s day occurs for which three readings are required, they shall do as we have stated for the octave of Saint John.

## CHAPTER XX. The octave of the apostles

At Vespers on the octave of the apostles, the antiphon shall be “You shall be blessed when people…” (*Beati eritis cum vos*). Psalms from the feria. Hymn: “With golden light” (*Aurea luce*). Antiphon: “These are the saints” (*Isti sunt sancti*). “Let us pray: O God, whose right hand” (*Deus cujus dextera*).

Invitatory: “Rejoice and exult” (*Gaudete et exsultate*), sung by two brothers in copes. Three lights before [Col. 1224B] the altar. Hymn: “Let heaven rejoice” (*Exsultet coelum*). Antiphons of the many apostles shall be taken. Readings shall be read from sermons of the holy Fathers. They shall sing the responsories mystically, taking one from the history of blessed Peter and another concerning the apostle Paul; all these shall be completed by singing wherever necessary. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be sung by two.

For the canticle, antiphon: “Glorious princes of the earth” (*Gloriosi principes terrae*). Gospel: “Jesus ordered his disciples” (*Jussit Jesus discipulos suos*). Homily by the same blessed Jerome.

At Lauds, antiphon: “This is my commandment” (*Hoc est praeceptum meum*), and the following antiphons. Hymn: “With golden light” (*Aurea luce*). Antiphon: “Holy and true light” (*Sanctum et verum lumen*).

If it is a Sunday, they shall celebrate the morning Mass of that Sunday, adding the collect of the apostles; otherwise, they shall celebrate a Mass from the apostles. At the principal office all the deacons and priests shall be in copes. Six lights shall be before the altar, together with those carried by the converts. Office: “The wisdom of the saints” (*Sapientia sanctorum*). “Let us pray: O God, whose right hand” (*Deus cujus dexteram*). Epistle: “These are men of mercy” (*Hi sunt viri misericordiae*). Responsory: “The souls of the just” (*Justorum animae*). Alleluia: “Let the just feast” (*Justi epulentur*). Gospel: “Jesus ordered” (*Jussit Jesus*). Office: “They shall exult” (*Exsultabunt*). Communion: “The souls of the just” (*Justorum animae*).

At Vespers, antiphon: “The rod of your power” (*Virgam virtutis tuae*). Psalms: “The Lord said” (*Dixit Dominus*); “let him place him” (*collocet eum*); “coming, they shall come” (*venientes venient*); “he was strengthened” (*confortatus est*); “Lord, you have examined me” (*Domine probasti me*). Responsory: “The apostle Peter and Paul” (*Petrus apostolus et Paulus*). Hymn: “With golden light” (*Aurea luce*). Antiphon: “These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands” (*Isti sunt duae olivae et duo candelabra*). “Let us pray: O God, whose right hand” (*Deus cujus dextera*).

## CHAPTER XXI. On the feast of Saint Peter ad Vincula

[Col. 1224D]

On the feast of Saint Peter in Chains, chapter reading: “Peter indeed was being kept in prison” (*Petrus quidem servabatur in carcere*). Responsory: “If you love me” (*Si diligis me*). Hymn: “Blessed Peter, bound by the snare of chains” (*Petrus beatus catenae laqueo*). “Whatever you bind” (*Quodcunque vinclis*). “Glory to God through endless ages” (*Gloria Deo per immensa*). The priest shall be in a cope and shall incense the altar.

Antiphon: “The angel of the Lord stood near” (*Angelus Domini adstitit*). Let it be sung a third time. “Let us pray: O God, who [made] blessed Peter the apostle” (*Deus qui beatum Petrum apostolum*).

Invitatory: “You are the shepherd of the sheep” (*Tu es pastor ovium*), sung by two brothers in copes. Hymn: “Let heaven rejoice” (*Exsultet coelum*).

In the first nocturn, antiphon: “Into all the earth” (*In omnem terram*). Four readings from the Acts of the Apostles: “King Herod sent forth his hands” (*Misit Herodes rex manus*). In the second, four other readings from a sermon of Saint Augustine: “You have heard, dearest brothers, the most blessed Peter” (*Audistis, fratres charissimi, beatissimum Petrum*).

They shall sing all the responsories from his history, beginning “Simon Peter” (*Simon Petre*) [Col. 1225A]. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be sung by two, and after the Gloria they shall repeat the twelfth from the beginning.

For the canticle, antiphon: “Herod sent” (*Misit Herodes*), or “The Lord sent an angel” (*misit Dominus angelum*). Canticle: “You saints of the Lord” (*Vos sancti Domini*). Homily from the Gospel, “Jesus came into the region” (*Venit Jesus in partes*). “In the white garment” (*In albam*) [Note: It should perhaps read *in alba*, that is, at dawn, or at Lauds.]: “But Peter was being kept” (*Petrus autem servabatur*). Antiphon: “Peter was sleeping” (*Erat Petrus dormiens*). Antiphon: “The angel of the Lord” (*Angelus Domini*). Hymn: “Blessed Peter” (*Petrus beatus*). Antiphon: “Whatever” (*Quodcunque*).

At the morning Mass, collects shall be said as in the twelve readings. At the main office everyone shall put on copes, including the converts who know how to sing. Candles shall be present before the altar for this sacred office. Six brothers shall hold the office. “Now I truly know” (*Nunc scio vere*). “Let us pray: O God, who [made] blessed Peter” (*Deus, qui beatum Petrum*). Epistle: “Herod sent” (*Misit Herodes*). Responsory: “You shall appoint them” (*Constitues eos*) [Col. 1225B], sung by two or three. Alleluia: “Release [him], at God’s command” (*Solve jubente Deo*), sung by four. Gospel: “Jesus came” (*Venit Jesus*). Office: “You shall appoint them” (*Constitues eos*). Two offertories shall be received. Communion: “Simon, son of John” (*Simon Joannis*).

At Vespers, antiphon: “The Lord has sworn” (*Juravit Dominus*), or his proper nocturnal antiphons. Hymn: “Blessed Peter” (*Petrus beatus*). Antiphon: “Simon Peter said to Jesus” (*Dixit Simon Petrus ad Jesum*), and the collect appointed for the day itself.

## FIRST SUNDAY OF AUGUST

On Saturday at Vespers, responsory: “Send forth, Lord” (*Emitte Domine*). At the Magnificat: “Wisdom has possessed me” (*Dominus possedit me*). Let them read from Solomon both in the church and at the meal until [supplement: “the beginning of”] September.

## CHAPTER XXII. The vigil of Saint Lawrence

[Col. 1225C]

On the vigil of Saint Lawrence, immediately after Sext, when the church custodian has sounded the bell, everyone shall rise from their beds, attend to their needs, and assemble and wash their hands and faces. The boys, without any sound of the bell, shall come into the church before the altar, make prayer, leave, and put on the sacred vestments appropriate for Mass. The priest with the ministers shall then celebrate the Mass of the vigil of that day. They shall not sing the Alleluia.

On that day they shall not eat suet, and in the refectory whatever remains of the bread and wine shall be received by the almoner. Before Vespers the church custodian shall adorn the altars with silks and spread carpets over the frames.

For the Vesper synaxis, let them place five candles before the altar. Chapter reading: “I will confess to you, Lord, King” (*Confitebor tibi, Domine rex*) [Col. 1225D]. Responsory: “Where are you going?” (*Quo progrederis*). Hymn: “Martyr of Christ” (*Martyris Christi*). Verse: “He distributed; he gave to the poor” (*Dispersit, dedit pauperibus*). Antiphon: “The deacon Lawrence” (*Levita Laurentius*). “Let us pray: Be present, O God, to our supplications” (*Adesto, Deus, supplicationibus*).

At the station, responsory: “The deacon Lawrence” (*Levita Laurentius*). “Let us pray: Stir up, Lord, in the church” (*Excita, Domine, in ecclesia*).

For the invitatory, four in copes shall sing “Blessed Lawrence” (*Beatus Laurentius*). Hymn: “With devoted mind” (*Devota mente*). Eight readings from his Passion. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth responsories shall, as usual, be repeated after the Gloria by the four in copes. In the first and second nocturns, three candles shall be before the altar and one behind. In the third, a homily of Saint Augustine: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat…” (*Amen, amen dico vobis, nisi granum frumenti*), and two candles shall be added.

After the Gospel has been recited: “Let us pray: Stir up, Lord” (*Excita, Domine*). At Lauds, at the station, responsory: “Blessed Lawrence” (*Beatus Laurentius*).

They shall celebrate the morning Mass of the Sunday, if it occurs, adding the prayer of Saint Lawrence: “Stir up, Lord” (*Excita, Domine*), and the other customary prayers. At the Hours they shall impose an antiphon from the morning praises without the verses.

At the principal Mass all the priests and deacons shall be clothed in copes. Seven candles shall be lit before the altar. “Let us pray: Grant, we beseech you, almighty God” (*Praesta, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus*).

At Vespers they shall impose the antiphon that was used at the nocturn, without the following verses. They shall take the psalms from the office of one martyr. Both at this Hour and at the morning office, one priest shall be in a cope to incense the altar.

They shall celebrate his octave with twelve readings. For the invitatory, two brothers in white: “The just man shall flourish” (*Justus florebit*). Antiphon and responsories as above in his sacred office. For we know that this repetition of the feast occurs during the octave of the most blessed Mary.

Let them read readings from the sermons of the holy Fathers [supplied: *sermonibus*]. Let them sing eight responsories from the history of the aforementioned saint. At the morning praises let them bring forth five antiphons, and at Terce celebrate the principal Mass from his office. Office: “Lord, you have examined my heart” (*Domine, probasti cor meum*). Collect: “Stir up, Lord” (*Excita, Domine*). Epistle: “He who sows peace” (*Qui pacem seminat*). Responsory: “You went before him” (*Praevenisti eum*). Alleluia: “This is truly a martyr” (*Hic est vere martyr*). Gospel: “If anyone wishes to come after me” (*Si quis vult post me venire*). Office: “In strength” (*In virtute*). Communion: “You have placed, Lord” (*Posuisti, Domine*).

If this octave occurs on a Sunday, [Col. 1226C] let them read eight readings about the blessed man himself and four others about the Sunday. Homily of the same day. The morning praises of that Sunday follow. At the collect, let them repeat the antiphon with Gloria concerning the aforementioned saint; then let them bring forth an antiphon concerning Saint Mary. If it seems suitable, let the third nocturn be celebrated concerning Saint Mary. But the Mass of the Sunday itself shall be celebrated on the weekdays.

## CHAPTER XXIII. Lead the whole feast of the Virgin’s Assumption in this manner with me

The vigil of the Assumption of Saint Mary. Before Prime, let them adorn the church, with curtains and hangings on both sides of the walls [Note: *Palliis*, with hangings, veils, or silks.]. Behind the backs of the brothers in the choir, let them arrange *bancalia* around it [Note: *Bancalia* are cloths placed over the seats or benches in the choir. Thus Durand, *Rationale*, book I, chapter 3, no. 23.]. Let them spread carpets over the frames. Let them adorn the altars with their ornaments. In the main church let them place all the prepared books, and twelve candles before it. Let the basilica of Saint Mary be most beautifully decorated both with hangings and with gold-woven banners [Note: *Phanones*, *fanones*, *fanen*: veils or standards.].

They shall celebrate the morning Mass of Saint Eusebius, adding other Masses for the dead. Everyone shall make the offertory. After the chapter meeting, let everyone come to be shaved.

After Sext, when they hear the signal, let them rise from their beds, wash their hands and faces, and let the boys go into the church without the sound of the bell. Let them pray, and let the priest put on the chasuble, the deacon the dalmatic, and the subdeacon the tunic [Col. 1227A]. The cantor shall be in the choir with a cope. Three converts shall be in white [dressed in white], two of whom shall carry candlesticks and the third a thurible. All the boys shall be in white. Two brothers in copes shall sing the responsory. Then all the bells shall be rung.

Three candles shall be arranged before the altar for this Mass. Office: “Hail, holy parent” (*Salve, sancta parens*). “Let us pray: O God, who [made] the virginal hall” (*Deus qui virginalem aulam*), and the other customary prayers. Readings from Wisdom: “I flourished like a vine” (*Ego quasi vitis fructificavi*). Responsory: “Blessed and venerable” (*Benedicta et venerabilis*). The Alleluia shall not be sung at this Hour. Gospel: “A certain woman, lifting up her voice” (*Extollens quaedam mulier*). Offertory: “Blessed indeed” (*Felix namque*), and half [that is, half the brothers] shall make the offertory, as they are accustomed to do on weekdays. Communion: “Blessed is the womb” (*Beata viscera*). On that day they shall not eat suet, and whatever remains in the refectory shall be received by the almoner [Col. 1227B].

At Vespers, first two small bells shall be rung, and afterward two bells at a time. Twelve candles shall be before the altar and ten behind. Antiphon over the psalms: “Rejoice and be glad” (*Gaude et laetare*). Psalms for the day itself. Chapter reading: “In all things, rest” (*In omnibus requiem*). Responsory: “Adorned with necklaces” (*Ornatam monilibus*). Hymn: “Who could with great…” (*Quis possit amplo*). Two priests shall put on copes to incense the altars around them.

Antiphon: “Holy Mary, pray always” (*Sancta Maria exora semper*), sung triumphally. “Let us pray: O God, who [made] the virginal hall” (*Deus qui virginalem aulam*). At the station, antiphon: “Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ” (*Mater Domini nostri Jesu Christi*); verse and whatever prayer concerning the blessed woman they wish.

Before the nocturnal office, before the bells are sounded, all the crowns [Note: Candlesticks made in the shape of a crown, as I said above.] shall be lit, together with three candles before the great altar and two behind. Then all the bells shall be rung until the boys arrive.

For the invitatory, four shall put on copes. Hymn: “Who could with great…” (*Quis possit amplo*), or “Christ’s accessible…” (*Christi pervia*). Let all the readings be taken from a sermon of Saint Jerome: “You compel me, O Paula” (*Cogitis me, o Paula*). Two and two shall sing the tracts.

In the first, second, and third nocturns, the priest shall put on a cope with an alb. When the reader has begun the third reading, the priest shall be ready in the sacristy, put incense into the thurible, and then come and incense only the great altar, and afterward the brothers in the choir in order.

For the canticles, fifteen candles shall be lit on a pole, nine before the altar, and seven behind it. The Gospel shall not be proclaimed [read perhaps: “with”]. After the Gloria, they shall repeat the twelfth responsory from the beginning. Gospel: “She was filled” (*Repleta est*). Prayer: “Venerable to us, Lord” (*Veneranda nobis, Domine*) [Col. 1227D].

At Lauds, responsory: “The holy Mother of God has been exalted” (*Exaltata est sancta Dei genitrix*). Hymn: “Most blessed light of the world” (*Lux mundi beatissima*). At the station, responsory: “Who is this?” (*Quae est ista*). Then the priest shall say the verse and the prayer from the Mass of the Virgin herself.

At the Hours, three candles shall be lit before the altar. Before Prime is sounded, all the ornaments, golden chalices, and two candlesticks shall be placed on the great altar; the candlesticks shall be lit in the same place and shall burn throughout the day.

The morning Mass shall be said in the basilica of Saint Mary, and only one collect shall be brought forth [Col. 1228A]. At the Sanctus, everyone, from the smallest to the greatest, shall be clothed in white. When it has been completed, they shall sound the bell and pray together. Only then shall they sound the bell and celebrate Terce.

The armarius and sacristan shall prepare themselves with the processional ornaments. Then two youths or boys shall go ahead and put on tunics to carry the Gospel books. Next the converts shall come: they shall take the candlesticks, two thuribles, one the incense material, and three crosses.

After this, four elders who possess sacred orders shall come, carrying the lesser relics; another shall walk outside these and take a panel with an image of our Lord Jesus Christ and of his Mother. Then [Col. 1228B] the *paraphonista* shall impose this antiphon: “You are altogether beautiful” (*Tota pulchra es*), and another: “How beautiful” (*Quam pulchra*).

Then let them come in order, as the following arrangement indicates:

Holy water, cross, thurible. Candles, candlestick, candles. Priest, scepter, arm, crucifix. Chest, text, text, glorious scepter. Cross, thurible, candlestick. Candles, panel, orb [Note: Hariulfus also mentions a golden orb among the sacred vessels and ornaments, book II, chapter 10. Bernard, however, in the *Consuetudines Cluniacenses*, mentions a wax orb that burns throughout the night; this cannot in any way be referred to in explaining this passage, but must be understood as a nocturnal light.].

Then the boys with their masters, followed by the lord abbot, then the priest and afterward the deacons, and finally the converts. As long as they come singing through the cloister, let them proceed in this order so that they may enter the church atrium without delay. When they have arrived there, let them stand in an ordered procession in the middle, as they came [Col. 1228C].

The elders shall assist, as is customary for them to stand in the choir. There they shall say this responsory: “Above salvation” (*Super salutem*). When it is finished, they shall enter the church singing this responsory: “Mary has been taken up into heaven” (*Assumpta est Maria in coelum*), while all the bells are sounding.

The church custodian shall provide copes for everyone and tunics for the boys. Once the bells have ceased, let the armarius have twelve copes prepared in the choir. Those to whom the abbot gives the signal shall put them on and begin the office with him: “Let us rejoice” (*Gaudeamus*).

The sacristan shall light twelve candles before the altar. Four shall sing the Gradual: “Because of truth” (*Propter veritatem*). Six shall sing the Alleluia: “Mary has been taken up” (*Assumpta est Maria*). Gospel: “Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit” (*Repleta est Spiritu sancto Elisabeth*), or “The Lord Jesus entered a certain village” (*Intravit Dominus Jesus in quoddam castellum*). “I believe in one God” (*Credo in unum Deum*). Two shall sing the offertories. When Mass has been completed, [Col. 1228D] all the bells shall be rung.

In the refectory, a threefold distribution of drink shall be made, as we stated for the Resurrection of the Lord; and in every respect everything shall be completed as they find it prescribed there.

At Vespers, antiphon: “While the king was at his table” (*Dum esset rex*). Psalms: “The Lord said” (*Dixit Dominus*). Antiphon: “His left hand” (*Laeva ejus*). “Praise, children” (*Laudate pueri*). “When I rejoiced” (*Laetatus sum*). Antiphon: “I am black” (*Nigra sum*). Psalm: “Unless” (*Nisi*). Antiphon: “Now winter” (*Jam hiems*). Psalm: “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem” (*Lauda, Hierusalem, Dominum*). Responsory: “The holy one has been exalted” (*Exaltata est sancta*). Hymn: “Who could with great…” (*Quis possit amplo*). In the Gospel, antiphon: “Today Mary” (*Hodie Maria*).

### During the octave

They shall not kneel. The bells shall be sounded as on ordinary weekdays. Invitatory: “Holy Mother of God” (*Sancta Dei genitrix*). Reading from a sermon of Saint Jerome. Responsory concerning the blessed woman herself. In each nocturn, one antiphon.

At Lauds one bell shall be rung, and they shall bring forth the psalms under one antiphon, one of these for each day: “Mary the Virgin has been taken up” (*Assumpta est Maria Virgo*); “Mary the Virgin, ever blessed” (*Maria Virgo semper benedicta*); “You are beautiful” (*Pulchra es*). Responsory: “She has been exalted” (*Exaltata est*).

When the commemoration of the saints has been completed, they shall come into the other choir and celebrate Lauds there. Then they shall return, going to rest in the dormitory if it is not yet day.

At Prime, a Mass for the dead shall be said. In the cloister they shall speak as on other days. At the Hours, nocturnal antiphons shall be taken that are suitable, whether from Lauds, the Gospel, or the Song of Songs [Col. 1229B].

When the church custodian has sounded the bell, everyone shall go and pray. Then those who have been permitted to serve at the sacred office shall put on white garments. When the bell sounds, they shall celebrate Terce. They shall not impose the psalms for household members at the ends of the Hours.

After Terce, they shall celebrate the office “Let us rejoice” (*Gaudeamus*), or “Your face” (*Vultum tuum*). Also another: “Hail, holy parent” (*Salve sancta parens*). Responsory: “Blessed and venerable” (*Benedicta et venerabilis*). Alleluia: “Because of truth” (*Propter veritatem*). Alleluia: “O how beautiful you are” (*O quam pulchra es*). Alleluia: “She has been taken up” (*Assumpta est*). Alleluia: “Today Mary” (*Hodie Maria*). Office: “She has been taken up” (*Assumpta est*). Alleluia: “Blessed indeed are you” (*Felix namque es*), or “Hail, Mary” (*Ave Maria*). Communion: “The Virgin Mary has been exalted” (*Exaltata est Virgo Maria*), or “Blessed is the womb” (*Beata viscera*). Alleluia: “You have loved” (*Dilexisti*).

Vespers shall be said under one antiphon, with ferial psalms. When the servants leave the refectory, let them celebrate the Office of the Dead [Col. 1229C]. If a saint’s day occurs for which three readings are to be celebrated, let them read a sermon about Saint Mary, bring forth a tract concerning the saint, say five antiphons at Lauds, and celebrate Mass from that saint’s office at Terce.

On Saturday, let the office be made for the holy cross. If a Sunday occurs, let everything be done concerning the blessed Virgin, and in the third nocturn let them proclaim the Gospel: “She was filled with the Holy Spirit” (*Repleta est Spiritu sancto*). If no saint’s day is present, let them celebrate the morning Mass from the Virgin’s office; during that week let them say the Sunday Mass [Note: That is, the Mass of the preceding Sunday.]. Likewise on Wednesday and Friday, adding the Gospels for those days as they are attached in the book.

## CHAPTER XXIV. The octave of Saint Mary

At the invitatory on the octave of Saint Mary, four shall be in copes and shall say this antiphon: “Come, let us adore the King of kings” (*Venite adoremus Regem regum*), or “Your fragrance, holy Mother of God” (*Odor tuus sancta Dei genitrix*). Psalm: “Come” (*Venite*). Hymn: “Christ’s gate is made” (*Fit porta Christi*).

In the first nocturn, the antiphons shall be said as at her feast. Eight readings from a sermon of Saint Jerome: “We read, therefore, how often at funerals and burials…” (*Legimus ergo quam saepe ad funera, et ad sepulturas*). Responsories concerning the blessed woman herself. Let them read the homily: “The Lord Jesus entered a certain village” (*Intravit Dominus in quoddam castellum*). This reading is connected with the preceding one in a most beautiful manner.

At Mass, offertory: “Let us all rejoice” (*Gaudeamus omnes*). “Let us pray: [For] your servants” (*Famulorum tuorum*). Reading: “In all things, rest” (*In omnibus requiem*). “Let us pray.” Gradual: “Because of truth” (*Propter veritatem*). Alleluia: “Today Mary the Virgin” (*Hodie Maria Virgo*), or “O how beautiful you are” (*O quam pulchra es*), or “Alleluia, she has been taken up” (*Alleluia, Assumpta est*). Another verse: “After childbirth, a Virgin” (*Post partum Virgo*). Whoever sings it shall say one after another. The clergy who hold the choir, or those standing at length, shall sing with the repetitions that belong there. Likewise the Sequence.

Gospel: “The Lord Jesus entered” (*Intravit Dominus Jesus*). Offertory: “She has been taken up” (*Assumpta est*). Communion: “The Virgin has been exalted” (*Exaltata est Virgo*).

At Vespers, the antiphons with the psalms shall be as at her feast.

## CHAPTER XXV. On the feast of Saint Bartholomew

At Vespers on the feast of Saint Bartholomew, carpets shall be arranged over the frames, and five candles shall be placed before the altar. Reading of one [supplement from another manuscript: “apostle”]. A short responsory shall be sung by the boys. At the steps [Col. 1230B] the priest shall be in a cope. “Let us pray: Almighty and eternal God” (*Omnipotens sempiterne Deus*).

At the station, responsory: “Citizens of God, of the apostles” (*Cives Dei Apostolorum*). Prayer concerning him.

For the invitatory, two in copes: “Rejoice” (*Gaudete*). Three candles before the altar. Readings and responsories concerning the blessed man. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be said by two. In the third [nocturn], a homily of blessed Gregory, pope, from the Gospel: “This is my commandment” (*Hoc est praeceptum meum*). Two candles shall be added at the altar.

At the station, responsory: “They were without complaint” (*Fuerunt sine querela*). Let them celebrate the morning Mass from his office. At the principal office all priests and deacons shall be surrounded by copes. Offertory: “But to me exceedingly” (*Mihi autem nimis*). Let the Gradual and everything else be done as it is contained in the feast of the apostles. Let them celebrate Vespers as is customary at the Nativity of one apostle. If this solemnity occurs on a Sunday, nevertheless let everything be done concerning the apostle [Col. 1230C].

## CHAPTER XXVI. On the feast of Saint Augustine

At Vespers: “Behold, a great priest” (*Ecce sacerdos magnus*). Antiphon: “In the midst of the church” (*In medio ecclesiae*). “Let us pray: Your church, Lord” (*Ecclesiam tuam, Domine*). At the station, responsory: “In the midst of the church” (*In medio ecclesiae*). The rest as at the feast of Saint John the Evangelist, with the prayer of a confessor.

Invitatory: “The King of Confessors, the Lord” (*Regem Confessorum Dominum*). Eight readings from his life: “Therefore, from the African province” (*Ex provincia ergo Africana*). Responsories from the office of confessors. The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be sung by the boys with Gloria.

Introit from a homily of Saint Gregory, from the Gospel: “A certain man went abroad” (*Homo quidam peregre*), or “Watch therefore” (*Vigilate itaque*). At the station: “Behold, truly an Israelite” (*Ecce vere Israelita*).

The morning Mass shall be said concerning him; or, if another saint is present [Col. 1230D], it shall be said concerning that saint. At the principal office: “In the midst of the church” (*In medio ecclesiae*). “Your church, Lord” (*Ecclesiam tuam, Domine*). Readings from Wisdom: “I desired, and it was given to me” (*Optavi, et datus est*). Responsories and everything else from the office of confessors.

## On the Nativity of Saint Julian the Martyr

For the invitatory, two shall be in copes. Psalm: “The just man shall flourish” (*Justus florebit*). Psalm: “Come” (*Venite*), and everything from the office of one martyr. Let the feast be celebrated as with two copes.

## CHAPTER XXVII. On the Beheading of Saint John

Before Vespers is sounded, let the altar dedicated in his name be beautifully adorned, and let one candle be placed before it; at the principal altar, five. Chapter reading: “The mockeries of the saints” (*Sancti ludibria*) [Col. 1231A]. Responsory: “The Lord’s Forerunner has come” (*Praecursor Domini venit*). Hymn: “Defender of justice” (*Assertor aequitatis*). Verse: “Great is his glory” (*Magna est gloria ejus*). Antiphon: “When John was questioned” (*Interrogatus Joannes*). “Let us pray: Of Saint John the Baptist and your martyr” (*Sancti Joannis Baptistae, et martyris tui*).

Then let them repeat the antiphon concerning Saint Mary Sabina [Note: *Savina*, *Sabina*, with *b* alternating with *v*.].

Two in copes shall say the invitatory: “The eternal and triune Lord” (*Aeternum, trinumque Dominum*). Hymn: “God of your people” (*Deus tuorum*). Antiphon: “For all the things that…” (*Ad omnia quae*). Also Alleluia: “When Herod heard” (*Audivit Herodes*), and the rest as they are set out in the authoritative book. Verses of one martyr shall be said.

Eight readings from a sermon of Saint John, bishop: “Today, as we celebrate the strength of John and the savagery of Herod” (*Hodie nobis Joannis virtus, Herodis feritas*). Responsory: “Herod sent” (*Misit Herodes*). The fourth, eighth, and twelfth shall be sung by two.

In the third nocturn, let the Gospel according to Matthew be proclaimed: “At that time, when Herod heard…” (*In illo tempore, audivit Herodes*) [Col. 1231B]. Homily of Bede the priest: “As we celebrate, dearest brothers, the birthday of blessed John” (*Natalem, fratres charissimi, beati Joannis diem celebrantes*).

Let two candles be added before the altar. At Lauds, responsory: “With glory and honor” (*Gloria et honore*). Hymn: “There was no prophet” (*Non fuit vatis*). Antiphon: “When Herod had sent” (*Misso Herodes*).

Let the morning Mass be celebrated concerning Saint Sabina, adding the collect of Saint John and the customary prayers. At the principal office, all ranks of priests and deacons shall be surrounded by copes. Seven lamps shall be lit. Offertory: “From my mother’s womb” (*De ventre matris meae*), held by six. “Let us pray: Of Saint John the Baptist” (*Sancti Joannis Baptistae*). Epistle: “The mockeries of the saints” (*Sancti ludibria*). Responsory: “Before…” (*Priusquam*), sung by two. Alleluia: “Among those born of women” (*Inter natos mulierum*), performed by three. Gospel: “Herod sent and held John” (*Misit Herodes ac tenuit Joannem*). Offertory: “Great is…” (*Magna est*), or “You have placed” (*Posuisti*). Communion: “You have placed, Lord” (*Posuisti, Domine*) [Col. 1231C].

In the refectory, let the tables be covered. At the Hours, chapter reading from the office of one martyr. Prayers from his Nativity, as appropriate, or take them from the office of a martyr. At Vespers, antiphons from the nocturn shall be said. Psalms of one martyr. Responsory: “You have placed, Lord” (*Posuisti, Domine*). Hymn: “Defender” (*Assertor*). Antiphon: “Blessed John stood in the middle of the prison” (*Medio carceris stabat beatus Joannes*). Prayer: “Of Saint John the Baptist” (*Sancti Joannis Baptistae*).

## CHAPTER XXVIII. The first Sunday of September

Here the short tract shall be suspended until Easter. On Saturday at Vespers, responsory: “Before I eat, I sigh” (*Antequam comedam suspiro*); antiphon at the Magnificat: “When Job had heard” (*Cum audisset Job*).

On Sundays and vigils, as well as at the daily meal hours, let them read the books of Job, Tobit, Judith, Esther, and Ezra, together with their commentaries, until the tract for the month of October is available. From these same books let the chants be sung.

### On the third Sunday: from the history of Tobit

On Saturday at Vespers, responsory: “O gentle father, bless” (*O mitis pater benedic*). At the Magnificat, antiphon: “Do not remember” (*Ne reminiscaris*). Reading at the vigil from the book of Tobit himself: “Tobit was from the tribe and city of Naphtali” (*Tobias ex tribu et civitate Nephtali*). Tract: “I ask, Lord” (*Peto Domine*).

### The fourth Sunday of September: from Judith

At the nocturnal office, first reading: “Now Arphaxad, king of the Medes…” (*Arphaxat itaque Rex Medorum*), and the following readings from the same book. Tract: “The tribulations of the city” (*Tribulationes civitatis*).

## CHAPTER XXIX. Let them celebrate the birth of the Theotokos in this manner, in the words of the servants

[Col. 1232A]

At the Nativity of Saint Mary, before Vespers is sounded, let the altars and the whole church be adorned. Before Vespers let them spread carpets over the frames. Let the presbytery and choir be adorned. Chapter reading: “A shoot shall go forth” (*Egredietur virga*). Responsory: “Of the glorious Virgin Mary” (*Gloriosae Virginis Mariae*). A hanging [Note: Something is missing here.], and let them fit coverings around the benches. Before the arch let them spread a hanging. Let them place all the Gospel books on the altar. Five candles shall be lit before it, three in the instrument, and only one at the other altars; and let them be decorated with silks, both these and those that are inscribed. Let them spread carpets over the frames.

Chapter reading: “A shoot shall go forth” (*Egredietur virga*). Responsory: “Of the glorious Virgin Mary” (*Gloriosae Virginis Mariae*), or “With heart and soul” (*Corde et animo*) [Col. 1232B]. Hymn: “Hail, star of the sea” (*Ave maris stella*). The priest shall incense the altars, surrounded by a cope. Antiphon: “Blessed indeed” (*Felix namque*). Verse: “Hail, Mary” (*Ave Maria*). Prayer: “The supplications of your servants” (*Supplicationes servorum tuorum*). Then let them repeat the antiphon concerning Saint Adrian at the station: “Blessed indeed” (*Felix namque*), verse “Hail, Mary” (*Ave Maria*), and the prayer of the blessed woman herself.

Invitatory: “The Nativity of the Virgin Mary” (*Nativitatem Virginis Mariae*), sung by four in the chapter. Hymn: “Whom earth and sea” (*Quem terra pontus*), or “Christ’s gate is made” (*Fit porta Christi*). Let three lights be lit before the altar and one behind it.

Let eight readings from the Song of Songs be read: “Let him kiss me” (*Osculetur me*), or readings from the approved customary source. Responsory: two shall bring forth the fourth, three the eighth, and four the twelfth; after the Gloria they shall repeat them from the beginning. For the canticle, fifteen candles shall be increased on a pole [Col. 1232C].

Let the Gospel be proclaimed: “The book of the genealogy” (*Liber generationis*), together with the exposition of Saint Jerome; from the same reading at Lauds. At the station, responsory: “The Nativity” (*Nativitatem*).

Let the morning Mass be of Saint Adrian. In the basilica of Saint Mary, let them hear the Mass and say the collect concerning her, and let them say the Alleluia. Customary prayer. At the principal office, all priests and deacons shall be surrounded by copes, and the boys by tunics.

Offertory: “Let us rejoice” (*Gaudeamus*), or “Hail, holy parent” (*Salve sancta parens*). Prayer: “The supplication” (*Supplicationem*). Reading: “The Lord possessed me” (*Dominus possedit me*). Responsory: “Blessed” (*Benedicta*), said by three. Alleluia: “Of the glorious Nativity” (*Nativitatis gloriosae*), sung by four. Gospel: “The book of the genealogy” (*Liber generationis*). Offertory: “Blessed indeed are you” (*Felix namque es*), and two shall receive the offertories. Communion: “Blessed is the womb” (*Beata viscera*).

As soon as Mass has been completed, all the bells shall be rung.

At Vespers, five candles shall be before the altar and three behind it [Col. 1232D]. Antiphon: “Blessed” (*Benedicta*). Psalm: “The Lord said” (*Dixit Dominus*). Antiphon: “Like myrrh” (*Sicut myrrha*). Psalm: “When I rejoiced” (*Laetatus sum*). Antiphon: “This is she who did not know” (*Haec est quae nescivit*). Psalm: “Unless the Lord” (*Nisi Dominus*). Antiphon: “From the fruit” (*De fructu*). Psalm: “Remember, Lord, David” (*Memento, Domine, David*). Reading: “My dove is one” (*Una est columba mea*). Responsory: “Today is the Nativity” (*Nativitas est hodie*). Hymn: “Now to you, Virgin” (*Nunc tibi virgo*). Antiphon: “Your Nativity” (*Nativitas tua*). Prayer: “To your servants” (*Famulis tuis*).

If the feast itself occurs on a Sunday, after the water has been blessed and “Sprinkle me” (*Asperges me*) has been sung, let them begin the responsory “Blessed is the offspring from whom Christ was born” (*Beata progenies unde Christus natus est*), or the antiphon “How beautiful they are” (*Quam pulchri sunt*). Let them proceed to Saint Mary, saying the prayer over the sick brothers. When the responsory has been completed: “Let us pray.” Let them say this sacred verse: “After childbirth, a Virgin” (*Post partum Virgo*). Prayer: “With supplications” (*Supplicationibus*). Through the cloister let them say the antiphons and responsories.

## CHAPTER XXX. On the Ides of September
In everything, let this always be begun by you. Let them perform Prime as before; finally, on that very day let them begin the fast which the Rule [Chapter 41] prescribes. After the chapter, let the board be sounded as it usually is on ordinary days, and let them speak until Terce is sounded. After Terce, while the brothers sit silently in the cloister, let the children and the sick come into the refectory. After Sext, let them go to the dormitory to rest; when the signal has been sounded, let them rise and attend to their needs [Col. 1233B]. When they have washed their hands and faces, let the children proceed without any sound into the church before the altar and pray together. Then let them rise, and let one of them say the litany. Let the priest go with the ministers to the sacristy, put on the sacred vestments, and perform the appointed duties—

After Mass, when the signal has been sounded, let them pray together; then those who are to serve the brothers should receive food, and after that interval, when None has been said, let them come to eat. After Vespers, let them say the Office of the Dead; then, when the little bell has been sounded, let them assemble to drink. On Wednesday and Friday let them make a procession. At the twelve lessons let them act as they usually do. Let them perform the remaining customary observances as above.

## CHAPTER XXXI. On the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

[Col. 1233C]

Let the altars be adorned with silks. In the middle of the high altar let prepared books be placed, and let five candles be lit; let carpets be arranged on the benches. At Vespers: lesson, “For this reason, think among yourselves” (*Hoc enim sentite in vobis*); responsory, “Above all the trees” (*Super omnia ligna*); hymn, “The banners of the King” (*Vexilla regis*); verse, “This sign of the cross” (*Hoc signum crucis*); antiphon, “O admirable Cross” (*O Crux admirabilis*); prayer, “O God, who [by] the Only-Begotten” (*Deus qui unigeniti*). Afterwards let the antiphon concerning the holy martyrs be said, with the *Gloria*.

Invitatory, “The King of Martyrs” (*Regem Martyrum*). Let two be in copes. Hymn, “The eternal gifts of Christ” (*Aeterna Christi munera*). In the first and second nocturns let them speak of the saints. Let two brothers chant the fourth, eighth, and twelfth responsories. At the canticle: antiphon, “Above all the cedars’ trees” (*Super omnia ligna cedri*). Alleluia, “Because of the wood we have become servants” (*Propter lignum facti sumus servi*), or “I heard” (*Audivi*). Let the *Gloria* be divided into three parts [Col. 1233D]. Let the Gospel, “Now is the judgment of this world” (*Nunc judicium est mundi*), be proclaimed, and let everything that follows be solemnly celebrated concerning the holy Cross.

At Lauds: responsory, “This sign of the cross” (*Hoc signum crucis*); hymn, “Blessed Cross” (*Crux benedicta*). At the station: antiphon, “Above all” (*Super omnia*). Let the morning Mass be said for the saints.

At Terce let all the brothers assemble dressed in albs. After Terce has been said, let them spread carpets before the altar. Let two deacons go to the place where the holy Cross had been set and carry it before the high altar, uncovering it and crying out this antiphon: “Behold the wood of the Cross” (*Ecce lignum crucis*). Immediately let all bend their knees. Let one part of the brothers come forward, prostrate themselves, pray first, and then kiss the Cross and the reliquary. Let the cantor begin the antiphon, while meanwhile they repeat, “We adore your Cross” (*Crucem tuam adoramus*), “O Lord” (*Domine*) [Col. 1234A]. Psalm, “May he have mercy on us” (*Misereatur nostri*). Let them repeat the antiphon throughout all the verses, while meanwhile the other antiphons are said: “O Cross more radiant” (*O crux splendidior*), “O green wood of the Cross” (*O crux viride lignum*).

After the Cross has been adored and raised before the altar, let the paraphonist immediately, together with the clergy, intone this antiphon: “Above all the cedars’ trees” (*Super omnia ligna cedrorum*), and let them place the Cross in its proper place. Then let copes be given to each of the brothers, and tunics to the children. Let them arrange a pallium and an alb on the high altar, together with seven candles, which are attended by the lay brothers present at Mass.

Then let the bells be rung, and let the Office begin: “In the name of the Lord, let every knee bend” (*In nomine Domini omne genu flectatur*). Let six brothers hold the choir. Prayer, “O God, who [by] the Only-Begotten” (*Deus qui unigeniti*). Epistle, “Christ became obedient for us” (*Christus factus est pro nobis*). Responsory, “Christ became obedient” (*Christus factus est*). Alleluia, “Sweet wood” (*Dulce lignum*) [Col. 1234B]. Let them chant the Gospel, “Now is the judgment of this world” (*Nunc judicium est mundi*), through “that you may be sons of light” (*Ut filii lucis sitis*). Offertory, “Protect us, O Lord” (*Protege, Domine*). Communion, “Through the sign of the Cross” (*Per signum crucis*).

At the Hours, let chapters, verses, and prayers be said that are suitable for this day itself. At Vespers let there be five lights, and let them perform this antiphon with the Psalms: “But we should glory” (*Nos autem gloriari*). Psalm, “The Lord said” (*Dixit Dominus*). “Savior of the world” (*Salvator mundi*). Psalm, “When you shall be” (*Cum fueris*). Antiphon, “We adore you, O Christ” (*Adoramus te, Christe*). Psalm, “Blessed” (*Beatus*). Antiphon, “Save us, O Christ” (*Salva nos, Christe*). Psalm, “Praise, servants” (*Laudate pueri*). Lesson, “Christ became obedient” (*Christus factus est*). Responsory, “This sign of the Cross” (*Hoc signum crucis*). Hymn, “The banners of the King” (*Vexilla regis*). Antiphon, “O blessed Cross” (*O crux benedicta*), or “Faithful Cross among all” (*Crux fidelis inter omnes*).

Afterwards let them say the antiphon concerning the preceding and following saints. If Sunday falls on this feast [Col. 1234C], let them do everything as has been prescribed above; likewise, let them adore the Cross while prostrate.

## CHAPTER XXXII. On the Fast of the Four Seasons

On Wednesday let them make a procession as usual. Let both lessons be read in the tone used for an epistle. Let them say a responsory for each. During these three days let them eat no fat.

On Friday let them likewise make a procession. On Saturday after Sext, as soon as they hear the signal, let them rise, attend to their needs, wash their hands and faces, and let the children go into the church without sound and pray together. When they rise, let the priest go before them into the sacristy and put on the chasuble [Col. 1234D], the deacon an alb and stole, and four brothers albs. Two of these are to chant the blessing, the alleluia, the verse, and the tract; lay brothers are to carry the candles, and all the children are to surround themselves with albs.

Let no lesson be said in this Mass. As soon as everything has been prepared, let the cantor come into the choir and begin the Office. Let the priest proceed to the altar, pray, and make confession with the levite; then let him say “Let us pray” and the collect, as it is contained in the sacramentary. Let the younger brothers read the lessons, and afterwards the seniors. Let the responsories likewise be chanted, beginning with one person and afterwards by the cantors in the choir . . . . from the beginning; nevertheless, let the verse be completed by the same person by whom it was begun.

Let two candles be lit before the altar, as on ordinary days. Lessons: “The Lord spoke” (*Locutus est Dominus*). Responsory, “Our protector” (*Protector noster*) [Col. 1235A]. Lesson, “The Lord spoke” (*Locutus est Dominus*). Responsory, “Turn back, O Lord” (*Convertere, Domine*), or “The word of the Lord came” (*Factum est verbum Domini*). Responsory, “Let my prayer be directed” (*Dirigatur*).

Let the lesson, “The angel of the Lord” (*Angelus Domini*), be read through “the cherubim and above, exalted forever” (*Cherubim et super exaltatum in saecula*). Then let the shorter blessing continue. When it has been completed, let the priest come to the altar, say “The Lord be with you,” and the prayer, “O God, who [saved] the three children” (*Deus qui tribus puerorum*). Let no other prayers follow.

After the epistle has been read, let him bring out the tract, “Praise the Lord, all nations” (*Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes*). Let only the abbot, or the person whom he orders, kiss the text and perform the offering. Those four brothers who chanted the blessing and the tract are to remove their vestments without any permission. Let one receive the peace if twelve lessons have been read that day concerning a saint.

For this Mass [Col. 1235B] let only one host be sent; and let the children not come forward to hold the Lord’s body for Communion, since they have done this at the Mass of the saint. In the refectory, let the almoner take whatever remains.

There are also four Saturdays on which fasts are established and the Offices of lessons and prayers are more extensive. The first is the Saturday in March, in the first month, according to the observance of Lent in springtime, when the month of new produce was reckoned among the Jews. The fourth month is June, on the second Saturday of the fast: on the Ides, the first fruits were offered to the Lord, and rest from work was observed that day. The seventh month is September, on the third Saturday, in autumn. This entire month was solemn, containing the days of expiation and the affliction of the soul, and the prohibition of servile work on the day of the Feast of Booths—that is, the setting up of tents—on the fifteenth day, for seven days. The tenth month is December, on the fourth Saturday, before the Lord’s Nativity; that is, four Saturdays beforehand.

In the same week, fasts and solemn celebrations of prayers and lessons must always be observed on Wednesday and Friday. On these days, in accordance with the decrees of Pope Gelasius, ordinations are carried out. These solemn observances of the four Saturdays are commonly called the “Twelve Lessons,” because with the lessons and the canticles or psalms that are sung, this number is completed.

## CHAPTER XXXIII. The Vigil of Saint Matthew

At the vigil of Saint Matthew the Apostle, as soon as the brothers hear the signal after Sext, let them rise, wash their hands [Col. 1235D] and faces, and then let the children go into the church without any sound. Let them say prayers before the altar and begin the lessons; for as soon as they have risen . . . .

Office, “But I, like an olive tree” (*Ego autem sicut oliva*). Prayer, “Grant us, almighty God” (*Da nobis, omnipotens Deus*), or from Wisdom, “Blessed is the man” (*Beatus homo*). Responsory, “The just man” (*Justus*). Gospel, “Jesus saw a tax collector named Levi” (*Vidit Jesus publicanum nomine Levi*). Offertory, “Glory and honor” (*Gloria et honore*). Communion, “You have placed, O Lord” (*Posuisti, Domine*).

For the Mass let them act as they usually do at the vigils of the apostles; and let them perform the almsgiving in the same way.

At Vespers: lesson, “How beautiful are the feet” (*Quam speciosi pedes*). Responsory, “When the living creatures breathe” (*Cum spiret animalia*). Hymn, “Let heaven exult” (*Exsultet coelum*). Antiphon, “The likeness” (*Similitudo*). Its proper prayer. Verse in copes, “Rejoice and exult” (*Gaudete et exsultate*). Let eight lessons be read concerning his passion. Let two brothers perform the fourth responsory [Col. 1236A], three the eighth, and four the twelfth, in the middle of the church. Let the homily for the day be proclaimed. Let two candles be added. At the station let them go to the holy Cross.

Let the morning Mass be sung there, with this Office: “The mouth of the just man” (*Os justi*), or from Wisdom, “Blessed is the man who has found” (*Beatus vir qui invenit*). Responsory, “Blessed is the man who fears” (*Beatus vir qui timet*). Alleluia, “I send you” (*Ego vos*). The Gospel concerning him. Offertory, “You have placed, O Lord” (*Posuisti, Domine*). Communion, “Great are you” (*Magnus es*).

At the greater Office let all the priests and levites be in copes, and the children in tunics. Let six hold the offertory in the middle of the church. Let five candles be lit in addition to those carried by the lay brothers. Collect, “Blessed Matthew” (*Beati Matthaei*). Epistle, “The likeness of a face” (*Similitudo vultus*). Let two brothers chant the responsory, “You will appoint them” (*Constitues eos*). Let them say the Alleluia three times. Verse, “To Zion” (*Ad Sion*). Gospel, “As Jesus was passing by, he saw a man sitting” (*Cum transiret Jesus, vidit hominem sedentem*) [Col. 1236B]. Offertory, “Into all the earth” (*In omnem terram*). Communion, “Great are you” (*Magnus es*).

At Vespers let there be five lights. Let them take the antiphons and psalms from the Office customary for the apostles [supplement: “Office”]. When these have been completed, let them say the antiphon concerning Saint Maurice and his companions.

If this feast falls during the fast of the Four Seasons, nevertheless let everything be celebrated as prescribed above. After the chapter, finally, let them sit in the cloister until the signal sounds at Terce; then let them go into the church, pray, and let all the priests and levites put on albs. After Terce has been said, let them surround themselves with copes and celebrate Mass as we have specified above.

At None let them perform the sacred Office of the fast, as is customary; and if only the vigil occurs, let them add only the collect for the dead. If the vigil falls on Saturday, let the morning Mass likewise be from the chapter, and let there be added from . . . the vigil of the fast. Let the morning Mass be celebrated for the apostle, and let the customary prayers for the living or the dead, “Your saints” (*Sanctorum tuorum*), be added [Col. 1236C].

## CHAPTER XXXIV. “Let all proceed with such joys of the heavenly host”

At the feast of Saint Michael, at Vespers: chapter, “There was silence” (*Factum est silentium*). Responsory, “In the sight of the angels” (*In conspectu angelorum*). Antiphon, “There was silence in heaven” (*Factum est silentium in caelo*). At the end of this canticle, let five [brothers] repeat the antiphon from the beginning three times. On that day alone let them say the prayer, “O God, who in wondrous order” (*Deus qui miro ordine*). Let one priest officiate at the censing of the altars. At the station: responsory, “A faithful saying” (*Fidelis sermo*) [Col. 1236D].

Invitatory: two in copes, “The King of archangels” (*Regem archangelorum*). Hymn, “O Christ, glory of the holy angels” (*Christe sanctorum decus angelorum*). Let there be three candles before the altar and one behind it.

In the first and second nocturns, let eight lessons be read from the homily of Saint Gregory on the Gospel, “Tax collectors approached Jesus” (*Accesserunt ad Jesum publicani*). Let them begin at the words, “For angels and human beings have a nature” (*Angelorum quippe et hominum naturam*). Canticle, “May God have mercy on us” (*Deus misereatur nostri*).

At the entrance, the homily of Saint Jerome on the Gospel, “His disciples approached Jesus, saying, ‘Who, do you think?’” (*Accesserunt ad Jesum discipuli ejus dicentes, Quis putas*). Let two brothers perform the fourth responsory, four the eighth, and five the twelfth. Let fifteen candles be lit on the pole, two additional ones before the high altar, and likewise outside; let one candle be lit at each altar.

[Col. 1237A]

At the morning Office: responsory, “Holy Michael the archangel, defend us in battle” (*Sancte Michael archangele, defende nos in praelio*). “Of the Father” (*Patris*). Verse, “So that we may not perish in the dreadful judgment” (*Ut non pereamus in tremendo judicio*). Hymn, “To you, Christ, splendor” (*Tibi Christe splendor*). Verse, “In the sight of the angels” (*In conspectu angelorum*). Antiphon, “While the sacred mystery” (*Dum sacrum mysterium*). Let it be tripled [variant: *triplicatur*] at the *Gloria*. Prayer, “O God, who in wondrous order” (*Deus, qui miro*).

At the station: responsory, “Of the archangel Michael” (*Archangeli Michaelis*). Let the first Mass in the morning be for Saint Michael, and let all the customary collects be said. Epistle, “And there was a battle” (*Et factum est praelium*). Lesson, “There was a battle” (*Factum est praelium*).

At the greater Mass let all the priests and levites adorn themselves with copes. Let two pallia and an alb be placed on the high altar. Let seven candles burn together with those carried by the lay brothers, and three behind. Let six hold the Office: “Bless the Lord” (*Benedicite Dominum*), or “God has signified” (*Significavit Deus*). Let no responsory be said [Col. 1237B]. Four alleluias; let them take two offertories.

For the offertory, let two brothers have two golden censers prepared. As soon as they have said, “Many incenses were given to him” (*Data sunt ei incensa multa*), let one of the censers be given to the priest so that he may cense the chalice. When he has received it, let two priests in copes go in front and stand on either side of the altar, holding two censers and censing the altar above until the repetition of the verse, “And the smoke rose” (*Et ascendit fumus*), has been completed by the cantors. Then let both go to the altars situated behind the high altar and cense them and the altar in the middle together. Then let each proceed to the other altars on either side, circling them with incense.

When Mass has been completed, let all the bells be sounded. At Vespers let five candles be lit before the altar [Col. 1237C]. Antiphon, “The angel stood” (*Stetit Angelus*). Psalm, “The Lord said” (*Dixit*). Antiphon, “Incense was given to him” (*Data sunt ei*). Psalm, “Blessed is the man” (*Beatus vir*). Antiphon, “The smoke rose” (*Ascendit fumus*). Psalm, “Praise, servants” (*Laudate pueri*). Antiphon, “In the sight of the angels” (*In conspectu Angelorum*). Psalm, “I will confess” (*Confitebor*). Responsory, “The angel stood” (*Stetit Angelus*). Hymn, “To you, Christ” (*Tibi Christe*). Antiphon at the *Magnificat*, “Most glorious prince” (*Princeps gloriosissime*).

## CHAPTER XXXV. On Saint Jerome

At Vespers: antiphon, “In the midst of the church” (*In medio ecclesiae*). Prayer, “Your Church, O God” (*Ecclesiam tuam, Deus*). Let eight lessons be read from his life. In the third nocturn, the exposition of Pope Saint Gregory on the Gospel, “A certain man went abroad” (*Homo quidam peregre*).

At Mass: Office, “In the midst of the church” (*In medio ecclesiae*).
